title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.0 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 3.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County. .Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage. Additional heavy rainfall should cause the river to reach major flood stage Friday. For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is occurring and Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 10.5 feet, Water covers many secondary roads near the river, limiting access to homes to boats or high terrain vehicles. Flooding of homes along secondary roads near the river becomes more significant. Water begins to encroach on State Road 46 near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 9.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 9.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 10.4 feet Sunday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 8.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Advisory
description: * WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and San Joaquin Counties. * WHEN...Until 445 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots, roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1253 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding. - The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local time): * Port Chicago: 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 9:10 AM Wed 11/18, 1.3 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM Thu 11/19, 1.6 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri 11/20, and 2.0 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat 11/21. * West Sacramento: 1.4 ft above normal (5.7 ft MLLW) at 12:09 PM Wed 11/18, 1.6 ft above normal (6.0 ft MLLW) at 12:37 PM Thu 11/19, 1.9 ft above normal (6.3 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM Fri 11/20, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat 11/21. * Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +6.5 ft at 11:00 AM Wed 11/18, +6.9 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19, +6.4 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20, and +6.8 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21. - These predictions include up to +2.1 feet of storm surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the San Francisco Bay and Delta. - Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at: * Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre dictions.html?id=9415144 * West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide predictions.html?id=9416131 * Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWMLB The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Central Brevard County in east central Florida... * Until 745 AM EST. * At 450 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 4 and 6.5 inches of rain have fallen over the past 12 hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Melbourne, Titusville, Rockledge, Cocoa, Cocoa Beach, Satellite Beach, Cape Canaveral, Merritt Island, Sharpes, Port Canaveral, Port Saint John, Titusville Airport, Patrick Space Force Base, Indian Harbour Beach, Jetty Park, Viera, Canaveral Groves, Suntree, South Patrick Shores and Palm Shores.

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWLOX The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... The Gifford burn scar in... North Central Santa Barbara County in southwestern California... * Until 330 AM PST. * At 124 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated heavy rain falling over the Gifford Burn Scar. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour, much of which may fall in 15 to 30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar may result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain in and around the Gifford Burn Scar. SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the Gifford Burn Scar in Santa Barbara County. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Highway 166 between Twitchell Dam and the Cuyama Valley.

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWLOX The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Southern San Luis Obispo County in southwestern California... Northwestern Santa Barbara County in southwestern California... * Until 300 AM PST. * At 105 AM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated heavy rain falling across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 0.75 to 1.25 inches in 1 hour, much of which may fall in 15 to 30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain. SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Santa Maria, Lompoc, Orcutt, Los Alamos, Sisquoc, Vandenberg Village and Mission Hills.

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 3:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 3:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.7 feet early Monday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWLOX The National Weather Service in Los Angeles/Oxnard has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.75 to 1.5 inches in 1 hour, much of which may fall in 15 to 30 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash flooding. SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Vandenberg Space Force Base, Orcutt and Vandenberg Village.
